votes.evidence:
Premise confirmed by tracing callers into the worktree.

Caller side (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py): `handle_task_run_saved` reads `pr_url = output.get("pr_url")` (line 91) and `repository = (task.repository or "").strip() or None` (line 106). `repository` is only used for the branch leg / `_start_review` (line 119); the Stamphog dispatch at lines 126-138 passes `pr_url`, `team_id`, `acting_user_id`, `signal_report_id`, `task_run_id` and never compares the URL's repo to `task.repository`. `_start_stamphog_review` (lines 209-234) and `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155) forward those values unchanged.

Task side (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py): `process_inbox_pr_review` (1112-1240) derives `repository` solely from `_parse_pr_url(pr_url)` (1130-1133), resolves the `StamphogRepoConfig` by that parsed repo (1137-1150), fetches the PR (1159), checks only `state == "open"` and a non-empty head sha (1167-1174), then stamps `{"trigger": "inbox", "signal_report_id", "task_run_id", "acting_user_id"}` straight from the arguments (1176-1181) and creates the ReviewRun with that provenance (1223-1230). It never loads `task_run_id`, never calls `find_signal_implementation_run`, `_is_bot_authored`, or the `head.repo.full_name == repo` fork check. Contrast the webhook carve-out in the same file (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, 144-217), which requires bot author (174), repo-native head (180-182), a team-scoped `find_signal_implementation_run` match for this exact repo+PR (194-205), and re-resolves the toggle.

Downstream effect: provenance disables the engine's guards. products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, 237-238 skips author-history lookups; products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_integration.py:1386-1420 demonstrates that this provenance alone yields a real APPROVE on a bot-authored draft PR.

Reachability of a mismatched pr_url: `output.pr_url` is caller-written. `TaskRunViewSet.set_output` (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1094-1119, `task:write` scope) takes a bare `JSONField` (serializers.py:671-674); `validate_set_output` only checks `task.json_schema` (facade/api.py:2123-2136); `set_task_run_output` (2139-2160) saves it with no repository check; `_apply_caller_output` protects only `pr_merged` (`_WEBHOOK_ATTESTED_RUN_OUTPUT_KEYS = frozenset({"pr_merged"})`, 1770). Only the webhook backstop (products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:169-186) enforces the same-repo, non-fork rule, and it runs only when the agent-side write did not already set the URL. So the sandboxed coding agent (or any task:write caller) can point a signals implementation run at any open PR in any repo the team has a synced Stamphog config for, including a fork PR or a human PR, and Stamphog will review it under the self-driving carve-out.

Tests: `_inbox_pr()` in products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:908-919 always uses `REPO` matching the pr_url; no test exercises a repo/task mismatch or a fork head.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (1) The receiver already verifies the task run is a real signals implementation (signal_report_id set, non-internal, receivers.py:96-105), so `task_run_id` is genuine. But that says nothing about whether `pr_url` belongs to that task's repository, which is the claim. (2) The repo-config lookup is team-scoped (tasks.py:1137-1145), so the PR must be in a repo the same team connected. This narrows the blast radius to the team's own Stamphog-enabled repos but does not stop an unrelated, human-authored, or fork PR in such a repo from being reviewed and approved with self-driving provenance. (3) Maybe the engine re-checks authorship: it does not, `self_driving_review=True` is exactly what turns those refusals off (activities.py:451). (4) Maybe `pr_url` is server-attested: only `pr_merged` is (facade/api.py:1770); `pr_url` is agent/caller supplied and the fork check exists only on the webhook backstop path. No guard, test, or call-site fact makes the mismatch unreachable. Severity set to should_fix rather than must_fix because triggering it needs a prompt-injected or misbehaving sandbox agent or an insider with task:write, and the impact is an unintended automated review/approval scoped to repos the team itself enabled; it remains a real gap in an invariant the same module enforces on its other entry path.

Code facts (worktree /Users/woutut/.worktrees/posthog/frozen-75215):

1. `process_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1110-1112) takes `team_id, pr_url, acting_user_id, signal_report_id, task_run_id`. It resolves the repo solely from `_parse_pr_url(pr_url)` (1129-1133) and picks `StamphogRepoConfig.objects.for_team(team_id).filter(repository__iexact=repository, ...)` (1137-1147). The fetched PR is checked only for `state == "open"` (1167) and a non-empty head sha (1171). `task_run_id` / `signal_report_id` are never loaded or compared; they are copied verbatim into `inbox_review` provenance (1176-1181) and stored on the ReviewRun (1223-1224). No `_is_bot_authored`, no `head.repo.full_name` check, no `review_mode` check, no `find_signal_implementation_run` call.

2. The receiver (products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:106-131) has `task.repository` in hand (`repository = (task.repository or "").strip()`, line 106) but calls `_start_stamphog_review(pr_url=..., team_id=..., acting_user_id=..., signal_report_id=..., task_run_id=str(instance.id))` (127-136) without it, and never compares the URL's owner/repo to `task.repository`. `queue_inbox_pr_review` (products/stamphog/backend/facade/api.py:128-155) forwards the five args unchanged.

3. `pr_url` is caller-writable: `PATCH .../set_output` with `required_scopes=["task:write"]` (products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1101-1118) -> `set_task_run_output` (products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:2139-2156) assigns the caller's output wholesale. The facade's own comment at 1764-1770 names "a `task:write` holder" as the threat model for output writes and 1778-1780 explicitly contemplates "when the caller points the run at a different `pr_url`". Every output save fires `handle_task_run_saved`.

4. The stamped provenance is load-bearing: products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451 sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, and the comment at 448-450 claims it "is set exclusively from the run's inbox provenance, which both trigger paths stamp only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run." That is true for the webhook path (`_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, tasks.py:144-217: bot-author, repo-native head, synced config, `find_signal_implementation_run` team recheck, resolver) and false for the initial path.

5. Test coverage: `test_inbox_carve_out_scope` (products/stamphog/backend/tests/test_tasks.py:830-870, ids fork_head_is_never_linked / team_mismatch_fails_closed) covers the webhook carve-out only. The initial-path tests (`test_inbox_receiver_leg_*`, test_tasks.py:992-1060) cover head dedupe, stale snapshot, closed PR; none exercise a PR URL whose repo differs from the task's repository or a human/fork-authored PR. `test_gates_skip_without_starting_a_review` rows (products/review_hog/backend/tests/test_inbox_trigger.py:271-279) use `_PR_URL` with repository "o/r" and never assert on repo agreement.

Net: a same-team `task:write` holder (or a prompt-injected sandbox agent) can point a non-internal signals TaskRun's `output.pr_url` at any open PR in a Stamphog-configured repo of that team; Stamphog then creates a run with inbox provenance for it, the engine runs with `self_driving_review=True` (bot/draft bypass), and the run records `signal_report_id`/`task_run_id` from an unrelated implementation. Blast radius is team-scoped (`for_team(team_id)` on the config lookup), which is why this is should_fix rather than must_fix. Overlaps with UB7 (same missing revalidation, different lines).
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) "pr_url is server-derived so it cannot mismatch" - false; `set_task_run_output` accepts the caller's `pr_url` wholesale and the facade comment at products/tasks/backend/facade/api.py:1778-1780 explicitly handles callers repointing `pr_url`. (b) "the repo-config lookup scopes it" - it scopes to the team only (tasks.py:1137-1147), not to the task's repository, so any configured repo in the same team qualifies. (c) "the engine re-checks identity" - activities.py:451 trusts the provenance flag; its comment asserts a positive link the initial path never performs. (d) "the webhook carve-out's checks cover it" - they run only on later synchronize/reopen/retarget deliveries (tasks.py:164-166 returns empty for other actions); the initial review is explicitly delegated to `process_inbox_pr_review`. (e) "an existing test guards it" - the only mismatch tests (fork head, team mismatch) target `_inbox_rereview_carve_out`, not the receiver leg. All refutations fail; the claimed gap is in the code. The premise "can review an unrelated PR" holds within a team; cross-tenant is not reachable, which caps severity.

votes.evidence:
Trigger is reachable in production with ordinary credentials; no guard exists on this path.

1. `output.pr_url` is caller-writable through two public endpoints. `products/tasks/backend/presentation/views/api.py:1092-1120` (`PATCH .../runs/<id>/set_output/`, scope `task:write`) and `partial_update` (`facade/api.py:2016-2043`, `"output"` is in the serializer's writable fields at `presentation/serializers.py:113,304`). `facade/api.py:2139-2160 set_task_run_output` and `facade/api.py:1773-1789 _apply_caller_output` only strip the webhook-attested `pr_merged` key; `pr_url` is stored verbatim. `validate_set_output` (`facade/api.py:2123-2136`) only checks `task.json_schema`. The repo itself documents this: `products/tasks/backend/temporal/code_workstreams/activities/load_pr_urls.py:26-31` — "`output.pr_url` is user-writable, and a team's GitHub App installation can usually reach far more repos than any one task targeted. Without this check a user could point `pr_url` at an arbitrary PR the installation can see" — and adds `_pr_url_belongs_to_task_repo` as the guard for Code Home. The sandbox agent (LLM-driven, prompt-injectable) writes through the same surface.

2. The receiver fires on every such save. `products/review_hog/backend/receivers.py:60-64` connects `handle_task_run_saved` to `TaskRun.post_save`; `:80-83` only skips saves whose `update_fields` exclude `output`; `:93` reads `output.get("pr_url")`; `:97-104` requires only `task.signal_report_id` and `not task.internal`; `:126-138` queues Stamphog with `pr_url` and `task_run_id` passed independently. `task.repository` (`:105`) is never compared with the URL on the Stamphog leg.

3. The Celery task never binds the URL to the run. `products/stamphog/backend/tasks/tasks.py:1129-1150` parses the repo from `pr_url` and resolves `StamphogRepoConfig` by that repo only (team-scoped, but a team may have many enabled repos). `:1176-1181` stamps `inbox_review` provenance straight from the caller's `signal_report_id`/`task_run_id` without loading the run; `:1217-1229` creates the `ReviewRun` with it. Contrast the webhook path: `tasks.py:190-203` calls `find_signal_implementation_run(repository=repo, pr_url=...)`, which in `products/tasks/backend/webhooks.py:37-39` filters `task__repository__iexact=repository`. That check exists only for later deliveries.

4. The provenance is what relaxes the gates. `products/stamphog/backend/temporal/activities.py:451` sets `self_driving_review=bool(output.get("inbox_review"))`, with the comment "it is set exclusively from the run's inbox provenance, which both trigger paths stamp only after positively linking the PR to a signals implementation run" — an invariant the initial path does not uphold. `tools/pr-approval-agent/review_pr.py:589-590` then allows drafts, and the approval branch (`activities.py` post-verdict, cited by UB6) posts a GitHub approval.

Prod scenario: a team member with `task:write` (or the sandbox agent after a prompt injection) PATCHes `output.pr_url` on a non-internal signals implementation run to any open PR in another repo the team has Stamphog-enabled, with the acting reviewer's `stamphog_review_inbox_prs` on. Stamphog reviews and can approve that unrelated PR under the self-driving carve-out.
votes.refutation: Attempted refutations: (a) "pr_url is server-written only" — false; `set_output` and `partial_update` accept it from any `task:write` holder, and `load_pr_urls.py:26` states it is user-writable. (b) "Team scoping contains it" — `StamphogRepoConfig.objects.for_team(team_id)` (tasks.py:1139) limits the blast radius to the same team's enabled repos, but does not tie the PR to the task's repository; that is exactly the gap. (c) "The webhook carve-out re-validates" — `_inbox_rereview_carve_out` runs only for later synchronize/reopen/retarget deliveries (tasks.py:167), not for the initial run created here. (d) "The engine re-checks identity" — it keys solely off `inbox_review` (activities.py:451). None hold; the finding's premise matches the code.
